source.prompt: Which CRMs have a free plan, and what are the limits on it?
source.note: real collected answer; brand, competitors and publishers are the specs the cycle was scored with

answer.text:
Here are some popular CRMs with **permanent free plans** (not just trials) and the main limits you’ll run into. Limits change often, so it’s worth checking the vendor’s pricing page before committing.

| CRM | Free plan limits | Best fit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| HubSpot | Up to **2 users** on the free account according to HubSpot’s current FAQ; up to **1,000 contacts** and **1 million records across other standard object types**; no time limit. | Startups, small businesses, teams wanting a polished all-in-one CRM |
| Zoho Corporation CRM | Up to **3 users**; about **5,000 records** on the free edition; advanced automation and customization require paid tiers. | Small sales teams needing customization |
| Freshworks Freshsales | Up to **3 users**; unlimited contacts are commonly included, but advanced workflows, automation, and some sales features are paid. | Small sales teams wanting simple pipelines and email tools |
| Bitrix24 | Free CRM with contact/deal management; limits include storage and feature restrictions (commonly **5 GB storage** on free plans; user limits/features have changed over time). | Teams wanting CRM plus collaboration/project features |
| Agile CRM | Up to **10 users** and around **1,000 contacts/companies**; automation and marketing features are limited. | Small companies combining CRM with basic marketing |
| EngageBay | Free tier commonly includes up to **15 users** and around **250 contacts**; larger databases and advanced marketing require paid plans. | Small teams needing CRM + marketing tools |
| Capsule CRM | Up to **2 users** and about **250 contacts**; limited reporting and customization. | Freelancers and very small businesses |

## Quick recommendations

- **Best overall free CRM:** HubSpot — strong interface, broad integrations, and a generous free feature set.
- **Best for a 2–3 person sales team:** Zoho CRM or Freshsales.
- **Best if you need many users without paying:** Bitrix24 or Agile CRM (check current user limits before rollout).
- **Best for marketing + CRM together:** HubSpot or EngageBay.

A few common free-plan tradeoffs:

- Automation/workflows are usually the first thing locked behind paid plans.
- Advanced reporting and forecasting are often limited.
- Email marketing sends, sequences, and integrations usually have caps.
- User limits matter more than contact limits once a team grows.

If you tell me your use case (solo freelancer, startup, sales team size, e-commerce, agency, etc.), I can narrow this to the best 2–3 options.

HSRSources
